```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)

#load w1 to w4
w1 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0001-Data copy.rda") # Wave I in-home
w2<- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0005-Data copy.rda") # Wave II in-home
w3 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0008-Data copy.rda") # Wave III in-home
w4 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0022-Data copy.rda") # Wave IV in-home

load("data w1 to w4/21600-0001-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # check the new object name, then rename it to w1
load("data w1 to w4/21600-0005-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # check the new object name, then rename it to w2
load("data w1 to w4/21600-0008-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # check, then rename to w3
load("data w1 to w4/21600-0022-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # check, then rename to w4

#This reassigns w1 through w4 to point at your actual dataframes instead of the leftover character strings.
w1 <- da21600.0001   # Wave I in-home
w2 <- da21600.0005   # Wave II in-home
w3 <- da21600.0008   # Wave III in-home
w4 <- da21600.0022   # Wave IV in-home

View(w4)

#check if data frames are properly saved 
class(w1)      # should return "data.frame" or "tbl_df"/"tbl"
dim(w1)        # should show rows x columns, e.g. 6504 x ~2700
names(w1)[1:10]  # peek at the first few column names to confirm it looks right

#since you no longer need the original da21600.xxxx objects once you've reassigned them to w1–w4, and they're large, you can free up memory:
rm(da21600.0001, da21600.0005, da21600.0008, da21600.0022)
gc()  # trigger garbage collection to actually reclaim memory



######## WEIGHTS #######################
#bruh some variable names are not in W1.....
names(w1)[grepl("^AID$", names(w1), ignore.case = TRUE)]
names(w1)[grepl("^AID$", names(w1), ignore.case = TRUE)]
names(w1)[grepl("CLUSTER", names(w1), ignore.case = TRUE)]
#okay the weights for each wave are in another file so need to load them in

#wave 1 weights (DS4)
weights <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0004-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # confirm the object name, e.g. da21600.0004
w1_weights <- da21600.0004
View(w1_weights)

#wave 2 weights (DS7)
weights_2 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0007-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # confirm the object name, e.g. da21600.0004
w2_weights <- da21600.0007
View(w2_weights)

#wave 3 weights (DS21)
weights_3 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0021-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # confirm the object name, e.g. da21600.0004
w3_weights <- da21600.0021
View(w3_weights)


#wave 4 weights (DS31)
weights_4 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0031-Data copy.rda")
ls()   # confirm the object name, e.g. da21600.0004
w4_weights <-da21600.0031
View(w4_weights)



#Each wave file has hundreds of variables. If you merge everything first, you end up with a dataset thousands of columns wide, which is slow and confusing. Instead, select your variables of interest from each wave first, keeping AID in every one:

#variables not present: 
    #GSWGT1,  # Wave I cross-sectional weight    
    #CLUSTER2,    # PSU variable (needed for all analyses)
    #REGION,      # stratification variable


w1_sub <- w1 %>% select(AID,        #participant ID
                         # --- your W1 variables here ---
                         # --- Race -----
                         H1GI5F,      # race (Other Hispanic)
                         H1GI6A,      # race (White)
                         H1GI6B,      # race (Black or African American)
                         H1GI6C,      # race (American Indian or Native American)
                         H1GI6D,      # race (Asian or Pacific Islander)
                         H1GI6E,      # race (Other)
                         # --- AGE ----
                        H1GI1Y,       # birth year
                        H1GI1M,
                        IYEAR,        #interview year
                        IMONTH,
                         PA12,        # parental education (from parent questionnaire)
                         PA55,       # family income
                        # ---- SEX ----
                        BIO_SEX,     #male/female/refused
   #------ Section 10: Feelings Scale (Depression) ------
                        H1FS1,        # You were bothered by things that usually don’t bother you.
                        H1FS2,        # You didn’t feel like eating, your appetite was poor.
                        H1FS3,        # You felt that you could not shake off the blues, even with help from your                                          family and your friends.
                        H1FS4,        # You felt that you were just as good as other people.        (REVERSE)
                        H1FS5,        # You had trouble keeping your mind on what you were doing.
                        H1FS6,        # You felt depressed.
                        H1FS7,        # You felt that you were too tired to do things.
                        H1FS8,        # You felt hopeful about the future.                         (REVERSE)
                        H1FS9,        # You thought your life had been a failure.
                        H1FS10,       # You felt fearful.
                        H1FS11,       # You were happy                                              (REVERSE)
                        H1FS12,       # You talked less than usual.
                        H1FS13,       # You felt lonely.
                        H1FS14,       # People were unfriendly to you
                        H1FS15,       # You enjoyed life.                                          (REVERSE)
                        H1FS16,       # You felt sad.
                        H1FS17,       # You felt that people disliked you.
                        H1FS18,       # It was hard to get started doing things.
                        H1FS19,      # You felt life was not worth living
                        #---------Parent Relationships-----------
  # ---- Section 16: Relations with Parents (autonomy / decision-making) ----
  H1WP1,    # Q1  Parents let you decide your own weekend-night curfew?
  H1WP2,    # Q2  Parents let you decide the people you hang around with?
  H1WP3,    # Q3  Parents let you decide what you wear?
  H1WP4,    # Q4  Parents let you decide how much TV you watch?
  H1WP5,    # Q5  Parents let you decide which TV programs you watch?
  H1WP6,    # Q6  Parents let you decide what time you go to bed on week nights?
  H1WP7,    # Q7  Parents let you decide what you eat?
  H1WP8,    # Q8  # of past 7 days a parent was in the room while you ate evening meal

  # ---- Section 16: closeness / caring / educational aspirations (MOTHER) ----
  H1WP9,    # Q9   How close do you feel to your mother?
  H1WP10,   # Q10  How much do you think she cares about you?
  H1WP11,   # Q11  How disappointed would she be if you did NOT graduate college? (1-5)
  H1WP12,   # Q12  How disappointed would she be if you did NOT graduate high school? (1-5)

  # ---- Section 16: closeness / caring / educational aspirations (FATHER) ----
  H1WP13,   # Q13  How close do you feel to your father?
  H1WP14,   # Q14  How much do you think he cares about you?
  H1WP15,   # Q15  How disappointed would he be if you did NOT graduate college? (1-5)
  H1WP16,   # Q16  How disappointed would he be if you did NOT graduate high school? (1-5)

  # ---- Section 16 Q17: activities done with MOTHER in past 4 weeks ----
  H1WP17A,  # Q17a  gone shopping
  H1WP17B,  # Q17b  played a sport
  H1WP17C,  # Q17c  gone to a religious service / church event
  H1WP17D,  # Q17d  talked about someone you're dating or a party you went to
  H1WP17E,  # Q17e  gone to a movie, play, museum, concert, or sports event
  H1WP17F,  # Q17f  had a talk about a personal problem you were having
  H1WP17G,  # Q17g  had a serious argument about your behavior
  H1WP17H,  # Q17h  talked about your school work or grades
  H1WP17I,  # Q17i  worked on a project for school
  H1WP17J,  # Q17j  talked about other things you're doing in school
  H1WP17K,  # Q17k  none of the above

  # ---- Section 16 Q18: activities done with FATHER in past 4 weeks ----
  H1WP18A,  # Q18a  gone shopping
  H1WP18B,  # Q18b  played a sport
  H1WP18C,  # Q18c  gone to a religious service / church event
  H1WP18D,  # Q18d  talked about someone you're dating or a party you went to
  H1WP18E,  # Q18e  gone to a movie, play, museum, concert, or sports event
  H1WP18F,  # Q18f  had a talk about a personal problem you were having
  H1WP18G,  # Q18g  had a serious argument about your behavior
  H1WP18H,  # Q18h  talked about your school work or grades
  H1WP18I,  # Q18i  worked on a project for school
  H1WP18J,  # Q18j  talked about other things you're doing in school
  H1WP18K,  # Q18k  none of the above

  # ---- Section 18****: warmth / communication / satisfaction (MOTHER) ----
  H1PF1,    # Q1   Most of the time, your mother is warm and loving toward you
  H1PF2,    # Q2   Your mother encourages you to be independent
  H1PF3,    # Q3   When you do wrong, your mother talks it through & helps you understand why
  H1PF4,    # Q4   You are satisfied with the way your mother and you communicate
  H1PF5,    # Q5   Overall, you are satisfied with your relationship with your mother

  # ---- Section 18: warmth / communication / satisfaction (FATHER) ----
  H1PF23,   # Q23  Most of the time, your father is warm and loving toward you
  H1PF24,   # Q24  You are satisfied with the way your father and you communicate
  H1PF25,    # Q25  Overall, you are satisfied with your relationship with your father
  
  #------ Section 35: Protective Factors ------
# Administered to ALL respondents
# Scale: 1 = not at all, 2 = very little, 3 = somewhat, 4 = quite a bit, 5 = very much
# (6 = does not apply; 96 = refused; 98 = don't know)

H1PR1,   # Q1  How much do you feel that adults care about you?
H1PR2,   # Q2  How much do you feel that your teachers care about you?
H1PR3,   # Q3  How much do you feel that your parents care about you?
H1PR4,   # Q4  How much do you feel that your friends care about you?
H1PR5,   # Q5  How much do you feel that people in your family understand you?
H1PR6,   # Q6  How much do you feel that you want to leave home?  [REVERSE CODE]
H1PR7,   # Q7  How much do you feel that you and your family have fun together?
H1PR8,   # Q8  How much do you feel that your family pays attention to you?


  H1PF25    # Q25  Overall, you are satisfied with your relationship with your father

)




# Merge weights into your already-built w1_sub
w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  left_join(
    w1_weights %>% select(AID, GSWGT1, CLUSTER2),
    by = "AID"
  )

View(w1_sub)

sapply(w1_sub, class)
```

```{r}
#Wave 2- excludes race and family income
w2_sub <- w2 %>% select(AID,        #participant ID
# =============================================================
# Add Health WAVE II In-Home Questionnaire
# Requested constructs (bare variable codes; comment = #question)
# Bare names work inside dplyr::select(df, ...) / tidyselect.
# (In base R, c(...) needs quotes — these are unquoted as you asked.)
# =============================================================

# ---- DEPRESSION : Section 10 Feelings Scale (CES-D, 19 items) ----
  H2FS1,   # Q1  bothered by things that don't usually bother you
  H2FS2,   # Q2  didn't feel like eating / poor appetite
  H2FS3,   # Q3  couldn't shake off the blues
  H2FS4,   # Q4  felt just as good as other people        (REVERSE)
  H2FS5,   # Q5  trouble keeping your mind on things
  H2FS6,   # Q6  felt depressed
  H2FS7,   # Q7  felt too tired to do things
  H2FS8,   # Q8  felt hopeful about the future            (REVERSE)
  H2FS9,   # Q9  thought your life had been a failure
  H2FS10,  # Q10 felt fearful
  H2FS11,  # Q11 were happy                                (REVERSE)
  H2FS12,  # Q12 talked less than usual
  H2FS13,  # Q13 felt lonely
  H2FS14,  # Q14 people were unfriendly to you
  H2FS15,  # Q15 enjoyed life                             (REVERSE)
  H2FS16,  # Q16 felt sad
  H2FS17,  # Q17 felt people disliked you
  H2FS18,  # Q18 hard to get started doing things
  H2FS19,   # Q19 felt life was not worth living


# ---- AGE : Section 1 (birth date) + interview date ----
  H2GI1M,  # Q1  birth month
  H2GI1Y,  # Q1  birth year
  IMONTH2, # interview month  (use with birth date to compute age)
  IYEAR2,   # interview year

# No pre-computed age variable lives in the questionnaire; age is
# derived from birth date and interview date (or use the constructed
# CALCAGE2 from the separate constructed-variables file).

# ---- PARENT EDUCATION : Sections 14 & 15 (resident parents) ----
  H2RM1,   # S14 Q1  How far in school did she [resident mother] go?
  H2RF1,    # S15 Q1  How far in school did he [resident father] go?
# Note: Wave II does NOT re-ask education for NON-resident bio parents.

# ---- PERSONALITY : Section 18 self-description items ----
  H2PF12,  # Q12 get what you want b/c you worked hard for it
  H2PF13,  # Q13 go out of your way to avoid problems
  H2PF14,  # Q14 difficult problems make you very upset
  H2PF15,  # Q15 decisions on "gut feeling" w/o thinking consequences
  H2PF16,  # Q16 after a solution, think about what went right/wrong
  H2PF17,  # Q17 have a lot of energy
  H2PF18,  # Q18 seldom get sick
  H2PF19,  # Q19 when sick, get better quickly
  H2PF20,  # Q20 well coordinated
  H2PF21,  # Q21 have a lot of good qualities
  H2PF22,  # Q22 physically fit
  H2PF23,  # Q23 have a lot to be proud of
  H2PF24,  # Q24 like yourself the way you are
  H2PF25,  # Q25 doing everything just about right
  H2PF26,  # Q26 feel socially accepted
  H2PF27,   # Q27 feel loved and wanted


# ---- PERSONALITY FACTORS : Section 18 dispositional-trait items ----
# (The trait-like subset; same battery as above. Pick whichever set
#  matches your construct — these read most like "factors".)
  H2PF28,  # Q28 you like to take risks
  H2PF29,  # Q29 you are independent
  H2PF30,  # Q30 you are shy
  H2PF31,  # Q31 you are assertive
  H2PF32,  # Q32 you are sensitive to others' feelings
  H2PF33,  # Q33 you are emotional
  H2PF34,  # Q34 you can determine what will happen in your life
  H2PF35,   # Q35 you live without much thought for the future


# ---- PEER NETWORKS : Section 20 Friends ----
# Suffix A–E = friend 1–5;  MF = male friend, FF = female friend.
  FR_FLAG2,                                  # # of nominations allowed (1 vs up to 5)
  H2MF1, H2FF1,                              # Q1  name/ID of 1st male / female friend
  H2MF3A, H2MF3B, H2MF3C, H2MF3D,           # Q3  additional male-friend nominations
  H2FF3A, H2FF3B, H2FF3C, H2FF3D,           # Q3  additional female-friend nominations
  # --- friend school-enrollment / network-lookup items (Q4–Q9) ---
  H2MF4A,H2MF4B,H2MF4C,H2MF4D,H2MF4E, H2MF5A,H2MF5B,H2MF5C,H2MF5D,H2MF5E,
  H2MF6A,H2MF6B,H2MF6C,H2MF6D,H2MF6E, H2MF7A,H2MF7B,H2MF7C,H2MF7D,H2MF7E,
  H2MF8A,H2MF8B,H2MF8C,H2MF8D,H2MF8E, H2MF9A,H2MF9B,H2MF9C,H2MF9D,H2MF9E,
  H2FF4A,H2FF4B,H2FF4C,H2FF4D,H2FF4E, H2FF5A,H2FF5B,H2FF5C,H2FF5D,H2FF5E,
  H2FF6A,H2FF6B,H2FF6C,H2FF6D,H2FF6E, H2FF7A,H2FF7B,H2FF7C,H2FF7D,H2FF7E,
  H2FF8A,H2FF8B,H2FF8C,H2FF8D,H2FF8E, H2FF9A,H2FF9B,H2FF9C,H2FF9D,H2FF9E,
  # --- friend interaction / tie items (Q11–Q15), the core network ties ---
  H2MF11A,H2MF11B,H2MF11C,H2MF11D,H2MF11E,  # Q11 went to friend's house, past 7 days
  H2MF12A,H2MF12B,H2MF12C,H2MF12D,H2MF12E,  # Q12 met after school to hang out, past 7 days
  H2MF13A,H2MF13B,H2MF13C,H2MF13D,H2MF13E,  # Q13 spent time together, past weekend
  H2MF14A,H2MF14B,H2MF14C,H2MF14D,H2MF14E,  # Q14 talked about a problem, past 7 days
  H2MF15A,H2MF15B,H2MF15C,H2MF15D,H2MF15E,  # Q15 talked on the phone, past 7 days
  H2FF11A,H2FF11B,H2FF11C,H2FF11D,H2FF11E,  # Q11 (female friends)
  H2FF12A,H2FF12B,H2FF12C,H2FF12D,H2FF12E,  # Q12 (female friends)
  H2FF13A,H2FF13B,H2FF13C,H2FF13D,H2FF13E,  # Q13 (female friends)
  H2FF14A,H2FF14B,H2FF14C,H2FF14D,H2FF14E,  # Q14 (female friends)

  H2FF15A,H2FF15B,H2FF15C,H2FF15D,H2FF15E   # Q15 (female friends)
)

# Merge weights into your already-built w2_sub
w2_sub <- w2_sub %>%
  left_join(
    w2_weights %>% select(AID, GSWGT2, CLUSTER2),
    by = "AID"
  )

View(w2_sub)

sapply(w2_sub, class)

```

```{r}
# =============================================================
# Step 1: Convert CES-D factor items to numeric (0-3 scale)
# Add Health CES-D items are labeled factors where level 1 =
# "(0) Never/rarely" — so as.numeric(x) - 1 recovers the true
# 0-3 scale. VERIFY this with levels() above before trusting it.
# =============================================================

factor_to_cesd_numeric <- function(x) {
  as.numeric(x) - 1
}

# ---- Wave 1: H1FS1-H1FS19 (19 items, excluding suicidality item per earlier discussion) ----
w1_cesd_items <- c("H1FS1","H1FS2","H1FS3","H1FS4","H1FS5","H1FS6","H1FS7",
                    "H1FS8","H1FS9","H1FS10","H1FS11","H1FS12","H1FS13",
                    "H1FS14","H1FS15","H1FS16","H1FS17","H1FS18")
                    # H1FS19 (suicidality item) intentionally excluded — see earlier note

w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(w1_cesd_items), factor_to_cesd_numeric))

# ---- Wave 2: H2FS1-H2FS19 (same structure as Wave 1) ----
w2_cesd_items <- c("H2FS1","H2FS2","H2FS3","H2FS4","H2FS5","H2FS6","H2FS7",
                    "H2FS8","H2FS9","H2FS10","H2FS11","H2FS12","H2FS13",
                    "H2FS14","H2FS15","H2FS16","H2FS17","H2FS18")
                    # H2FS19 excluded for consistency with W1

w2_sub <- w2_sub %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(w2_cesd_items), factor_to_cesd_numeric))

# ---- Wave 3: H3SP5-H3SP13 (9 items) ----
w3_cesd_items <- c("H3SP5","H3SP6","H3SP7","H3SP8","H3SP9",
                    "H3SP10","H3SP11","H3SP12","H3SP13")

w3_sub <- w3_sub %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(w3_cesd_items), factor_to_cesd_numeric))

# ---- Wave 4: H4MH18-H4MH27 (9 items, skipping Q21) ----
w4_cesd_items <- c("H4MH18","H4MH19","H4MH20","H4MH22","H4MH23",
                    "H4MH24","H4MH25","H4MH26","H4MH27")

w4_sub <- w4_sub %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(w4_cesd_items), factor_to_cesd_numeric))


# =============================================================
# Step 2: Reverse-code the positively-worded items
# Formula for a 0-3 scale: reversed = 3 - x
# =============================================================

# ---- Wave 1 reverse items: H1FS4, H1FS8, H1FS11, H1FS15 ----
w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(
    H1FS4_r  = 3 - H1FS4,    # "felt as good as other people"
    H1FS8_r  = 3 - H1FS8,    # "felt hopeful about the future"
    H1FS11_r = 3 - H1FS11,   # "were happy"
    H1FS15_r = 3 - H1FS15    # "enjoyed life"
  )

# ---- Wave 2 reverse items: H2FS4, H2FS8, H2FS11, H2FS15 ----
w2_sub <- w2_sub %>%
  mutate(
    H2FS4_r  = 3 - H2FS4,
    H2FS8_r  = 3 - H2FS8,
    H2FS11_r = 3 - H2FS11,
    H2FS15_r = 3 - H2FS15
  )

# ---- Wave 3 reverse item: H3SP7 ----
w3_sub <- w3_sub %>%
  mutate(
    H3SP7_r = 3 - H3SP7    # "felt just as good as other people"
  )

# ---- Wave 4 reverse items: H4MH20, H4MH24, H4MH25 ----
w4_sub <- w4_sub %>%
  mutate(
    H4MH20_r = 3 - H4MH20,   # "felt just as good as other people"
    H4MH24_r = 3 - H4MH24,   # "felt happy"
    H4MH25_r = 3 - H4MH25    # "enjoyed life"
  )
```

# Manually check one row by hand
w1_sub %>%

  slice(1:5) %>%

w2_sub <- w2_sub %>%
  mutate(cesd_w2 = rowSums(select(., H2FS1, H2FS2, H2FS3, H2FS4_r, H2FS5,
                                       H2FS6, H2FS7, H2FS8_r, H2FS9, H2FS10,
                                       H2FS11_r, H2FS12, H2FS13, H2FS14,
                                       H2FS15_r, H2FS16, H2FS17, H2FS18),
                                na.rm = FALSE))
summary(w2_sub$cesd_w2)#***

w3_sub <- w3_sub %>%
  mutate(cesd_w3 = rowSums(select(., H3SP5, H3SP6, H3SP7_r, H3SP8, H3SP9,
                                       H3SP10, H3SP11, H3SP12, H3SP13),
                                na.rm = FALSE))
summary(w3_sub$cesd_w3)

w4_sub <- w4_sub %>%
  mutate(cesd_w4 = rowSums(select(., H4MH18, H4MH19, H4MH20_r, H4MH22,
                                       H4MH23, H4MH24_r, H4MH25_r, H4MH26,
                                       H4MH27),
                                na.rm = FALSE))
summary(w4_sub$cesd_w4)


#Step 2: Average the sums to account for different scales across questions. W1/W2 use an 18-item CES-D subset (range 0–54) while W3/W4 use a 9-item subset (range 0–27). Summed scores aren't on the same metric across waves, which is a real problem for growth modelling — a "high" score at W1 isn't comparable to a "high" score at W3 purely because there are half as many items. The standard fix is to convert each wave's sum to a mean score per item (sum ÷ number of items) rather than a raw sum, so all four waves sit on the same 0–3 scale

cesd_w1_mean = w1_sub$cesd_w1 / 18
cesd_w2_mean = w2_sub$cesd_w2 / 18 
cesd_w3_mean = w3_sub$cesd_w3 / 9
cesd_w4_mean = w4_sub$cesd_w4 / 9
#!!! use means for analyses

#Age
#Growth curve modelling needs a consistent time variable across all waves, and given Add Health's unequal wave spacing, age-at-interview is the right choice over wave number.

# Wave 1 — H1GI9 is already age, confirm it's numeric

w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(
    IYEAR_num  = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(IYEAR), "\\d{4}")),
    H1GI1Y_num = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(H1GI1Y), "\\d{4}")),
    age_w1 = (IYEAR_num - H1GI1Y_num))
summary(w1_sub$age_w1)

# Wave 2 — construct from birth date + interview date
w2_sub <- w2_sub %>%
  mutate(
    IYEAR2_num  = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(IYEAR2), "\\d{4}")),
    H2GI1Y_num = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(H2GI1Y), "\\d{4}")),
    age_w2 = (IYEAR2_num - H2GI1Y_num))
summary(w2_sub$age_w2) #w2 took place 1 yr after w1

w2_sub$IYEAR2

# Wave 3 — already have CALCAGE3, just rename for consistency
w3_sub <- w3_sub %>% mutate(age_w3 = as.numeric(CALCAGE3))
summary(w3_sub$CALCAGE3)

# Wave 4 — construct from birth date + interview date

  mutate(
    IYEAR4_num  = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(IYEAR4), "\\d{4}")),
    H4OD1Y_num = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(H4OD1Y), "\\d{4}")),
    age_w4 = (IYEAR4_num - H4OD1Y_num))
summary(w4_sub$age_w4)

                  H1PF1, H1PF2, H1PF4, H1PF5,
                  H1PF23, H1PF24, H1PF25), ~ as.numeric(.))) %>%
  mutate(parent_closeness = rowMeans(
    select(., H1WP9, H1WP10, H1WP13, H1WP14,

```{r}
#Predictor composites
#Right now you have individual items for protective factors, parent relationships, and personality, but no composite scores. For a growth model where these are time-invariant predictors of intercept/slope (most likely all measured at W1, since that's your baseline), you need single scores per construct

# Protective factors (H1PR1-H1PR8, watch for H1PR6 reverse-coding —
# "want to leave home" runs opposite to the other items)
w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(protective_factors = rowMeans(select(., H1PR1, H1PR2, H1PR3, H1PR4,
                                                    H1PR5, H1PR6_r, H1PR7, H1PR8),
                                        na.rm = TRUE))

# Parent relationship/closeness — decide which sub-block you actually want
# (closeness items H1WP9/10/13/14 are conceptually different from the
# autonomy items H1WP1-8 and the joint-activity checklist items H1WP17/18 —
# don't average all of them into one score without checking they load together)
w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(parent_closeness = rowMeans(select(., H1WP9, H1WP10, H1WP13, H1WP14,
                                                  H1PF1, H1PF2, H1PF4, H1PF5,
                                                  H1PF23, H1PF24, H1PF25),
                                      na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r fix-cesd-w3}
w3_sub <- w3_sub %>%
  mutate(cesd_w3 = rowSums(select(., H3SP5, H3SP6, H3SP7_r, H3SP8, H3SP9,
                                       H3SP10, H3SP11_r, H3SP12, H3SP13),
                            na.rm = FALSE))
summary(w3_sub$cesd_w3)
```

```{r fix-cesd-means}
w1_sub <- w1_sub %>% mutate(cesd_w1_mean = cesd_w1 / 18)
w2_sub <- w2_sub %>% mutate(cesd_w2_mean = cesd_w2 / 18)
w3_sub <- w3_sub %>% mutate(cesd_w3_mean = cesd_w3 / 9)
w4_sub <- w4_sub %>% mutate(cesd_w4_mean = cesd_w4 / 9)

# check: all four should sit on roughly 0-3
summary(w1_sub$cesd_w1_mean)
summary(w2_sub$cesd_w2_mean)
summary(w3_sub$cesd_w3_mean)
summary(w4_sub$cesd_w4_mean)
```


```{r composite-protective}
prot_items <- w1_sub %>%
  select(H1PR1, H1PR2, H1PR3, H1PR4, H1PR5, H1PR6_r, H1PR7, H1PR8)

prot_alpha <- psych::alpha(prot_items)
prot_alpha$total$raw_alpha          # report this value
# prot_alpha                        # uncomment for item-level / alpha-if-dropped

w1_sub <- w1_sub %>%
  mutate(protective_factors = rowMeans(prot_items, na.rm = TRUE))

summary(w1_sub$protective_factors)
```

```{r personality-scale-check}
# Confirm the response scale (expect 1-5) on a few items before reversing
table(w4_sub$H4PE1,  useNA = "always")
table(w4_sub$H4PE9,  useNA = "always")
table(w4_sub$H4PE29, useNA = "always")
```

```{r personality-reverse}
# Ensure numeric
ipip_items <- c("H4PE1","H4PE2","H4PE4","H4PE5",
                "H4PE9","H4PE10","H4PE11","H4PE12","H4PE13",
                "H4PE17","H4PE18","H4PE19","H4PE20","H4PE21",
                "H4PE25","H4PE26","H4PE27","H4PE28","H4PE29")
w4_sub <- w4_sub %>% mutate(across(all_of(ipip_items), ~ as.numeric(.)))

# Reverse-keyed items (6 - x on a 1-5 scale)
w4_sub <- w4_sub %>%
  mutate(
    H4PE9_r  = 6 - H4PE9,    # Extraversion (R)
    H4PE25_r = 6 - H4PE25,   # Extraversion (R)
    H4PE10_r = 6 - H4PE10,   # Agreeableness (R)
    H4PE26_r = 6 - H4PE26,   # Agreeableness (R)
    H4PE11_r = 6 - H4PE11,   # Conscientiousness (R)
    H4PE27_r = 6 - H4PE27,   # Conscientiousness (R)
    H4PE12_r = 6 - H4PE12,   # Neuroticism (R)
    H4PE28_r = 6 - H4PE28,   # Neuroticism (R)
    H4PE13_r = 6 - H4PE13,   # Openness (R)
    H4PE21_r = 6 - H4PE21,   # Openness (R)
    H4PE29_r = 6 - H4PE29    # Openness (R)
  )
```

```{r personality-subscales}
# Score each trait as the mean of its 4 items (C uses 3 confirmed items).
w4_sub <- w4_sub %>%
  mutate(
    extraversion      = rowMeans(select(., H4PE1, H4PE9_r,  H4PE17, H4PE25_r), na.rm = TRUE),
    agreeableness     = rowMeans(select(., H4PE2, H4PE10_r, H4PE18, H4PE26_r), na.rm = TRUE),
    conscientiousness = rowMeans(select(., H4PE11_r, H4PE19, H4PE27_r),        na.rm = TRUE),
    neuroticism       = rowMeans(select(., H4PE4, H4PE12_r, H4PE20, H4PE28_r), na.rm = TRUE),
    openness          = rowMeans(select(., H4PE5, H4PE13_r, H4PE21_r, H4PE29_r), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

psych::alpha(select(w4_sub, H4PE1, H4PE9_r,  H4PE17, H4PE25_r), check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha
psych::alpha(select(w4_sub, H4PE2, H4PE10_r, H4PE18, H4PE26_r), check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha
psych::alpha(select(w4_sub, H4PE11_r, H4PE19, H4PE27_r),        check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha
psych::alpha(select(w4_sub, H4PE4, H4PE12_r, H4PE20, H4PE28_r), check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha
psych::alpha(select(w4_sub, H4PE5, H4PE13_r, H4PE21_r, H4PE29_r), check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha

summary(select(w4_sub, extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, neuroticism, openness))
```

```{r age-check}
lapply(list(w1=w1_sub$age_w1, w2=w2_sub$age_w2,
            w3=w3_sub$age_w3, w4=w4_sub$age_w4), summary)
```

```{r trim-and-region}
# If REGION isn't already in w1_sub, merge it from the W1 weights object.
# (Adjust object name if different in your environment.)
if (!"REGION" %in% names(w1_sub) && exists("w1_weights") && "REGION" %in% names(w1_weights)) {
  w1_sub <- w1_sub %>% left_join(select(w1_weights, AID, REGION), by = "AID")
}

w1_keep <- w1_sub %>%
  select(AID, cesd_w1_mean, age_w1,
         protective_factors, parent_closeness,
         any_of(c("GSWGT1","CLUSTER2","REGION","BIO_SEX",
                  "H1GI6A","H1GI6B","H1GI6C","H1GI6D","H1GI6E","H1GI5F",
                  "PA12","PA55")))

w2_keep <- w2_sub %>%
  select(AID, cesd_w2_mean, age_w2, any_of(c("GSWGT2")))

w3_keep <- w3_sub %>%
  select(AID, cesd_w3_mean, age_w3, any_of(c("GSWGT3")))

w4_keep <- w4_sub %>%
  select(AID, cesd_w4_mean, age_w4,
         extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, neuroticism, openness,
         any_of(c("GSWGT4")))
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# MERGE the trimmed waves. Now there's exactly one CLUSTER2, one REGION,

# and one of each weight --- no .x/.y duplication to untangle.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r merge}
combined <- w1_keep %>%
  left_join(w2_keep, by = "AID") %>%
  left_join(w3_keep, by = "AID") %>%
  left_join(w4_keep, by = "AID")

dim(combined)
names(combined)
```

```{r restrict}
combined <- combined %>% filter(!is.na(GSWGT4))
nrow(combined)
```

```{r svydesign}
install.packages("survey")
library(survey)
options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")

addhealth_design <- svydesign(
  id      = ~CLUSTER2,
  weights = ~GSWGT4,
  data    = combined,
  nest    = TRUE
)
addhealth_design
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# FINAL READINESS CHECK. After this, you're clear to fit the LGC.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r final-check}
# The four repeated outcomes the growth model will use:
summary(select(combined, cesd_w1_mean, cesd_w2_mean, cesd_w3_mean, cesd_w4_mean))

# Time-invariant predictors:
summary(select(combined, protective_factors, parent_closeness))

# W4 personality mediators:
summary(select(combined, extraversion, agreeableness,
                          conscientiousness, neuroticism, openness))

# Missingness overview per analysis variable
colSums(is.na(select(combined,
  cesd_w1_mean, cesd_w2_mean, cesd_w3_mean, cesd_w4_mean,
  protective_factors, parent_closeness,
  extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, neuroticism, openness)))

# Save analysis-ready dataset
saveRDS(combined, "combined_analysis_ready.rds")
```

```{r}
cor(combined$protective_factors, combined$parent_closeness, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Same thing with a significance test and confidence interval
cor.test(combined$protective_factors, combined$parent_closeness)

```

  mutate(
    H1PF1_r  = 6 - H1PF1,

w1
